findings.title: Lighthouse 100/100/100/100 claim has no artifact anywhere in the repository
findings.quote: Mobile pit wall Lighthouse 13.4.1: 100/100/100/100 on mobile and desktop presets.
findings.why_wrong: A repo-wide search for "Lighthouse" finds only this line, two handoff notes, and scripts/dev/serve_mobile_pit_wall.mjs:1 ("Serve the mobile pit wall exactly as the worker does, on localhost, for Lighthouse."). The runner referenced by docs/handoffs/CLAUDE_HANDOFF_2026-09-17.md:305 (scripts\dev\lighthouse_mobile_pit_wall.ps1) is not in the tree at all, and the output location the handoffs name (outputs\lighthouse\) does not exist and is excluded by .gitignore:77 (`outputs/`). No Lighthouse JSON, no HTML report, no score record is committed, and .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml never runs Lighthouse. The claim sits in a file that ships to end users.
findings.impact: A perfect-score accessibility/performance/SEO/best-practices claim is made in a shipped validation document with zero retained evidence, in a project whose own rule (CONTRIBUTING.md:145-147) is "Do not claim ... validation without direct evidence. Write what was run and what was not." If a contrast or ARIA regression has since landed in the pit wall, nobody can tell, because no baseline exists to diff against.
findings.fix: Either commit the Lighthouse JSON (and the missing lighthouse_mobile_pit_wall.ps1 runner) under a non-ignored path with its SHA-256 recorded the way V1_RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md:24-27 requires of other evidence, or replace VALIDATION_REPORT.txt:8 with a dated statement naming the report file held outside the repo - the treatment lines 17-20 already give the executable and installer results.
findings.verifier_notes: The central supporting claim is false. The finder writes "The runner referenced by docs/handoffs/CLAUDE_HANDOFF_2026-09-17.md:305 (scripts\dev\lighthouse_mobile_pit_wall.ps1) is not in the tree at all" - it is in the tree: `ls scripts/dev` lists lighthouse_mobile_pit_wall.ps1, and its line 13 writes `Join-Path $repo ("outputs\lighthouse\{0}-mobile-pit-wall" ...)`. So the run is reproducible by a documented script. What remains true is that VALIDATION_REPORT.txt:8 "  Mobile pit wall Lighthouse 13.4.1: 100/100/100/100 on mobile and desktop presets." has no committed artifact, because outputs/ is ignored (.gitignore:77) and CI never invokes Lighthouse. That is ordinary treatment of a generated report, and the report's own lines 17-20 state that artifact-level results are recorded separately. Reduced to low. | The finding's load-bearing assertion is factually wrong. It states "The runner referenced by docs/handoffs/CLAUDE_HANDOFF_2026-09-17.md:305 (scripts\dev\lighthouse_mobile_pit_wall.ps1) is not in the tree at all." It is in the tree - `ls scripts/dev/` shows lighthouse_mobile_pit_wall.ps1 alongside serve_mobile_pit_wall.mjs, and I read it. It is not a stub: it serves the real worker page via serve_mobile_pit_wall.mjs, runs both presets (lines 26-36 `--only-categories=performance,accessibility,best-practices,seo`, `--preset=desktop`), and its own header states "Exit code 1 when any category scores below 100 or a run produced no report" - a hard gate, committed and re-runnable. That the JSON/HTML land in outputs\lighthouse\ and .gitignore:77 excludes `outputs/` is ordinary build-output hygiene, not absent evidence; the same is true of every other artifact this project produces. The claimed failure - "nobody can tell, because no baseline exists to diff against" - is not constructible when a one-command committed gate regenerates and re-asserts the scores.

findings.title: licenses.mjs fabricates a copyright holder and synthesises an MIT grant the package never published
findings.quote:
const holder = /github\.com\/facebook\//.test(repo) ? "Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates" : meta.author?.name ?? meta.author ?? `the ${name} authors`;
      body = `(The package declares MIT in package.json and ships no licence file; text reproduced from the SPDX identifier.)\n\n${mitText(holder)}`;
findings.why_wrong: When a dependency declares MIT but ships no LICENSE file, this branch writes a complete MIT grant into a shipped legal document with a copyright line the tool invented. The committed output proves it fired: apps/shell/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:7-14 carries `@astryxdesign/core 0.5.2  [MIT]` with "Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates" - a holder and a year-less notice derived from a regex on the repository URL, not from anything the package states. The final fallback is worse: `the ${name} authors` manufactures a copyright holder that is not a legal entity. Asserting the text and terms of a licence grant on the copyright owner's behalf is not a formatting convenience; if the owner's actual notice differs, the shipped file misstates the terms under which the code is redistributed.
findings.impact: apps/shell/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt is shipped as an Electron extraResource (apps/shell/scripts/package.mjs:37) into {app}\shell on every install. It currently tells recipients that Meta granted MIT terms for @astryxdesign/core in words Meta did not write. Any future MIT dependency without a licence file gets a notice attributed to "the <package> authors", which attributes a grant to nobody.
findings.fix: Delete the synthesis branch (lines 64-70). When a production package ships no licence file, push it onto `missing` so the generator throws (line 84) and the packaging check at apps/shell/scripts/package.mjs:14 blocks the build; then obtain the real notice from the package's repository and check it into an apps/shell/licences/<name>.txt override directory the generator reads verbatim.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed verbatim at apps/shell/scripts/licenses.mjs:69-70: `const holder = /github\.com\/facebook\//.test(repo) ? "Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates" : meta.author?.name ?? meta.author ?? `the ${name} authors`;` followed by the synthesised body. The committed output proves it fired: apps/shell/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:7-14 carries `@astryxdesign/core 0.5.2  [MIT]` and `Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates`, a holder derived only from a regex on the repository URL. The only mitigation is the parenthetical at line 70 disclosing that the text came from the SPDX identifier, which discloses the synthesis but does not make the invented holder line accurate. package.mjs:37 ships the file as an extraResource, so it reaches users. | Confirmed in both the generator and its committed output. apps/shell/scripts/licenses.mjs:64-70 is entered when `files.length` is 0 and `info.license === "MIT"`, and line 69 reads `const holder = /github\.com\/facebook\//.test(repo) ? "Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates" : meta.author?.name ?? meta.author ?? `the ${name} authors`;` - a copyright holder derived from a regex over the repository URL, with a final fallback naming no legal entity. It has fired: apps/shell/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt lines 7-14 carry `@astryxdesign/core 0.5.2  [MIT]`, the parenthetical "(The package declares MIT in package.json and ships no licence file; text reproduced from the SPDX identifier.)" and `Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates` with no year. That file is shipped verbatim to every install via package.mjs:37 extraResource, and apps/shell/test/licenses.test.mjs:18-20 asserts the committed file equals `render()`, so the synthesised text is pinned as correct. Asserting a grant's wording and holder on the owner's behalf in a distributed legal notice is the defect claimed.

findings.title: "Copyleft components" section omits every MPL-2.0 dependency in the release environment
findings.quote:
`pygame-ce` (LGPL-2.1) and `pystray` (LGPL-3.0) are used unmodified. The
packaged application keeps pygame-ce's compiled modules and the SDL2 libraries
as separate files under `_internal\pygame`; pystray is bundled as bytecode in
the application archive.
findings.why_wrong: sbom.cdx.json records three MPL-2.0 components this section does not mention: certifi 2026.7.22 licensed MPL-2.0, tqdm 4.70.0 licensed "MPL-2.0 AND MIT", and pathspec 1.1.1 whose licence text in THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:2285-2290 is verbatim "Mozilla Public License Version 2.0". certifi and tqdm are both transitive dependencies of openai, which src/ssc_engineer/voice/tts_backend.py:28 imports, and neither appears in the PyInstaller excludes list (ssc_race_engineer.spec:97-112), so both are frozen into the shipped executable. MPL-2.0 section 3.2 requires that when Covered Software is distributed in Executable Form the distributor informs recipients how to obtain the Source Code Form under the MPL. The notices do this for the two LGPL components and nothing else.
findings.impact: The shipped compliance document presents an exhaustive-looking copyleft inventory that misses two weak-copyleft components actually inside the binary. A downstream reviewer relying on this section concludes the product carries only LGPL obligations and will not provide the MPL source offer, leaving certifi's and tqdm's section 3.2 obligation unmet on every installer.
findings.fix: Extend THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:140-147 to a full weak-copyleft list: name certifi (MPL-2.0) and tqdm (MPL-2.0 AND MIT) as bundled, state that pathspec (MPL-2.0) is a build-time tool excluded from the binary (ssc_race_engineer.spec:103), and add the MPL section 3.2 source offer pointing at the exact PyPI sdist versions and hashes already in requirements-release.lock.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed by parsing sbom.cdx.json: certifi 2026.7.22 [MPL-2.0], tqdm 4.70.0 [MPL-2.0 AND MIT], and pathspec 1.1.1 whose reproduced text at THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:2287 is "Mozilla Public License Version 2.0". THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:140-147 names only pygame-ce and pystray under "## Copyleft components". Checked the one plausible mitigation: pathspec IS excluded from the freeze (ssc_race_engineer.spec:103 `"pathspec",`), so that one is out of the binary - but certifi and tqdm are not in the excludes list (97-112) and are openai transitive deps, so the finding's two named MPL components are genuinely shipped and genuinely undisclosed. | Verified by parsing sbom.cdx.json: certifi 2026.7.22 is licensed `MPL-2.0` and tqdm 4.70.0 `MPL-2.0 AND MIT`; THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:108 and :13935 carry the matching section headers. Neither name appears in ssc_race_engineer.spec's excludes (lines 97-112 list agents.voice, librt, mypy, mypy_extensions, numpy, pathspec, pygame.examples, pygame.tests, pytest, ruff and the pystray backends), and both are transitive dependencies of openai, which the app imports, so both are frozen into the shipped binary. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:140-149 is headed `## Copyleft components` and discusses only pygame-ce and pystray, providing the source offer for those two and nothing else. MPL-2.0 s3.2 obliges the distributor of Executable Form to inform recipients how to obtain Source Code Form; that notice is absent for two components actually inside the .exe. (The finding also cites pathspec, which is in the excludes list and therefore not frozen - that leg is wrong, but certifi and tqdm carry the finding.)

findings.title: Four shipped components are labelled NOASSERTION in the SBOM and in the installed licence file, including an MPL-2.0 one
findings.why_wrong: This block belongs to pathspec (sbom.cdx.json:877). Four components carry NOASSERTION (lines 223, 431, 873, 1133 - colorama, jaraco-classes, pathspec, pyinstaller-hooks-contrib), and because collect_third_party_licenses.py:58-63 copies that string straight into the section header, THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt ships `colorama 0.4.6  [NOASSERTION]` (line 218), `jaraco-classes 3.4.0  [NOASSERTION]` (line 828), `pathspec 1.1.1  [NOASSERTION]` (line 2285) and `pyinstaller-hooks-contrib 2026.7  [NOASSERTION]` (line 8850). The licence bodies reproduced immediately below each header identify the real licences unambiguously: colorama is BSD-3-Clause ("Copyright (c) 2010 Jonathan Hartley / All rights reserved. / Redistribution and use in source and binary forms..."), jaraco-classes is MIT, pathspec is MPL-2.0. In CycloneDX, NOASSERTION means the producer makes no statement about the licence - the opposite of what THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:124-125 claims.
findings.impact: The machine-readable SBOM installed alongside the application (installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss:60) reports "licence unknown" for four shipped components, one of which is weak copyleft. Any automated licence scanner run against sbom.cdx.json flags four unresolved components and cannot clear the release, and the human-readable file repeats the same non-answer.
findings.fix: In scripts/release/lock_release_dependencies.py, fall back to the wheel's `Classifier: License ::` entries and its dist-info licence files when License-Expression/License metadata is absent, and normalise to SPDX ids (colorama -> BSD-3-Clause, jaraco-classes -> MIT, pathspec -> MPL-2.0, pyinstaller-hooks-contrib -> "Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later"). Add an assertion in tests/release/test_third_party_licenses.py that no component's licence is NOASSERTION.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed exactly. sbom.cdx.json:870-877 is the block quoted and belongs to pathspec; parsing the file gives precisely four NOASSERTION components - colorama 0.4.6, jaraco-classes 3.4.0, pathspec 1.1.1, pyinstaller-hooks-contrib 2026.7. collect_third_party_licenses.py:58-63 concatenates the SBOM licence name straight into the section header, and `grep -n NOASSERTION THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` returns those four headers at lines 218, 828, 2285 and 8850, with the real licence text reproduced underneath (pathspec's is the MPL 2.0 verbatim). Contradicts THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:124-125 "The SBOM records every selected distribution, version, artifact hash, package URL identity and metadata-reported licence." | Verified programmatically: exactly four sbom.cdx.json components carry a NOASSERTION licence name - colorama, jaraco-classes, pathspec, pyinstaller-hooks-contrib. collect_third_party_licenses.py:58-63 builds the header from `entry["license"].get("id") or entry["license"].get("name", "")`, so the string propagates verbatim, and I confirmed the resulting headers in the committed file: `colorama 0.4.6  [NOASSERTION]` (line 218), `jaraco-classes 3.4.0  [NOASSERTION]` (828), `pathspec 1.1.1  [NOASSERTION]` (2285), `pyinstaller-hooks-contrib 2026.7  [NOASSERTION]` (8850). Both artifacts are installed (installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss:56 and :60). A licence scanner reading the SBOM gets "no assertion" for four shipped components, which is a real and repeatable result, and pathspec's reproduced body is the MPL-2.0 text. Note the impact overstates one point: pathspec is in the PyInstaller excludes (ssc_race_engineer.spec:104) so it is not in the frozen binary, but it is still declared as a shipped component in the installed SBOM, which is the defect.

findings.title: The shipped SBOM claims to be the complete inventory but omits the entire Electron/Node graph the same installer deploys
findings.quote:
A deterministic CycloneDX 1.5 inventory of all 67
direct and transitive distributions is supplied in `sbom.cdx.json` and installed
alongside the application.
findings.why_wrong: sbom.cdx.json contains exactly 67 components and all 67 are PyPI distributions (I parsed every purl; each is pkg:pypi/...). Since this branch, installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss:68 also installs the packaged Electron shell, whose apps/shell/pnpm-lock.yaml resolves 134 packages - 18 of them production dependencies that Vite bundles into the shipped renderer, plus the Electron runtime with its Chromium and Node.js component trees. None of that is in the SBOM. BUILD_INFO.txt:7 compounds it: "Dependencies           : requirements-release.lock and matching CycloneDX SBOM (unchanged)" is stated for a build whose installed footprint gained a Chromium.
findings.impact: The SBOM installed at {app}\sbom.cdx.json describes roughly half of what the installer actually put on disk. If a Chromium or Electron CVE lands, a vulnerability scan driven by this SBOM returns clean while the affected binary sits in {app}\shell - exactly the failure mode SBOMs exist to prevent.
findings.fix: Generate a second CycloneDX document for the shell (cyclonedx-npm against apps/shell with --omit dev, plus an explicit Electron component carrying its Chromium/Node versions), ship it via the existing extraResource list in apps/shell/scripts/package.mjs:37, and update THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:103-107 and BUILD_INFO.txt:7 to name both documents.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:105-107 reads "A deterministic CycloneDX 1.5 inventory of all 67 / direct and transitive distributions is supplied in `sbom.cdx.json` and installed / alongside the application." I parsed the SBOM: exactly 67 components, all purl-prefixed pkg:pypi. installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss:66-69 conditionally installs the packaged shell to {app}\shell, and apps/shell/pnpm-lock.yaml holds 134 `resolution:` entries with 8 declared production dependencies whose transitive closure Vite bundles. BUILD_INFO.txt:7 "Dependencies           : requirements-release.lock and matching CycloneDX SBOM (unchanged)" compounds it. The scan-blind-spot impact is accurate. | Confirmed by parsing the file: sbom.cdx.json has exactly 67 components and every purl is pkg:pypi (Counter gave {'pkg:pypi': 67}). installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss:68 `Source: "{#MyShellDir}\*"; DestDir: "{app}\shell"; Flags: ignoreversion recursesubdirs createallsubdirs` installs the packaged Electron app, and apps/shell/package.json declares eight production dependencies (@astryxdesign/core, @astryxdesign/theme-neutral, @fontsource/geist-mono, @fontsource/geist-sans, @stylexjs/stylex, lucide-react, react, react-dom) plus their transitives and the Electron/Chromium/Node runtime. None of that is in the SBOM installed at {app}\sbom.cdx.json (installer line 60). Concrete failure: a Chromium CVE lands, a scan driven by the installed SBOM returns clean, and the affected binary is sitting in {app}\shell. (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:105 does say "distributions", a Python term, so the wording is less absolute than the finding implies - but the scanning gap is real.)

findings.title: docs/README.md claims tooling verifies five release files against VERSION; release_metadata checks none of them
findings.quote:
Release metadata that tooling verifies against `VERSION` stays at the repository root:
`README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `BUILD_INFO.txt`, `VALIDATION_REPORT.txt`,
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` (generated), `requirements-release.lock`,
`sbom.cdx.json`.
findings.why_wrong: src/ssc_engineer/release_metadata.py:44-59 defines the complete set of version bindings and it contains exactly four entries: README.md's `# SSC Race Engineer v...` heading, README.md's `| Package | ` table row, BUILD_INFO.txt's `Package version : ...` line, and docs/user/QUICKSTART.txt's banner. CHANGELOG.md, VALIDATION_REPORT.txt, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt, requirements-release.lock and sbom.cdx.json are never matched against VERSION anywhere in the module - the only other place they appear (lines 106-122) is a check that the installer and spec mention the filenames, which is a packaging check, not a version check.
findings.impact: This is the mechanism behind the stale VALIDATION_REPORT.txt: a maintainer who reads docs/README.md believes `python -m ssc_engineer.release_metadata .` will catch a forgotten version bump in the validation report, runs the gate, sees it pass, and ships. It also means a version bump can leave CHANGELOG.md and the SBOM's application component pointing at the previous release with a green gate.
findings.fix: Either extend the `bindings` tuple in src/ssc_engineer/release_metadata.py:44-59 to cover VALIDATION_REPORT.txt's title line, CHANGELOG.md's top version heading and sbom.cdx.json's metadata.component.version, or correct docs/README.md:11-14 to list only the four files the checker actually binds and mark the rest as updated by hand at release time.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed by reading both files. docs/README.md:11-14 is quoted verbatim. src/ssc_engineer/release_metadata.py:46-63 defines `bindings` with exactly four entries - README.md heading, README.md package-contract row, BUILD_INFO.txt `Package version`, docs/user/QUICKSTART.txt banner - and lines 64-72 raise only on those. The only other appearance of the named files is `shipped_dependency_evidence` at lines 108-123, which asserts `filename not in definition` against the installer and spec text: a packaging-presence check, not a version check, exactly as the finder states. | Confirmed. docs/README.md:11-14 reads "Release metadata that tooling verifies against `VERSION` stays at the repository root: `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `BUILD_INFO.txt`, `VALIDATION_REPORT.txt`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` (generated), `requirements-release.lock`, `sbom.cdx.json`." I read release_metadata.py:45-59 in full: the `bindings` tuple has exactly four entries - README.md `^# SSC Race Engineer v([^\s]+)$`, README.md `^\| Package \| `([^`]+)`.*\|$`, BUILD_INFO.txt `^Package version\s+:\s+([^\s]+)$`, and docs/user/QUICKSTART.txt's banner - and lines 106-122 only assert that six filenames appear as strings inside installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss and ssc_race_engineer.spec (`shipped_dependency_evidence`), which is a packaging check with no version comparison. Six of the eight listed files are never matched against VERSION. This is the demonstrated mechanism behind finding 5's stale report, so the failure is not hypothetical - it already happened.

findings.title: CHANGELOG claims six palettes "pass WCAG AA" when only seven colour-contrast pairs are tested
findings.quote: header and each passes WCAG AA by test.
findings.why_wrong: The test behind this is apps/shell/test/themes.test.mjs:25-33, which checks exactly seven ratios per palette: primary and secondary text on body and surface, on-accent text on accent, and the accent as large text on body and surface. That is WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum) for a hand-picked token subset - nothing more. Level AA additionally requires keyboard operability (2.1.1), visible focus (2.4.7), non-text contrast (1.4.11), reflow (1.4.10), text spacing (1.4.12), name/role/value (4.1.2) and around forty other criteria, none of which any test in apps/shell/test/ exercises. The test does not even cover every text colour in the theme - disabled text and the status/warning/error foregrounds are not in the `checks` array. PRODUCT.md:103 scopes the same claim correctly ("WCAG AA contrast ... is already enforced by tests"); the changelog line drops the qualifier.
findings.impact: "Passes WCAG AA by test" in a changelog is the sentence a team quotes to a sponsor or an accessibility reviewer. The repository cannot substantiate it, and a reviewer who checks tab order or focus visibility in the Electron shell will find nothing has been verified - damaging exactly the evidence-discipline positioning PRODUCT.md:38-44 stakes the product on.
findings.fix: Change CHANGELOG.md:22 to "each meets the WCAG AA contrast minimum for its text and accent tokens by test", matching PRODUCT.md:103, and extend the `checks` array in apps/shell/test/themes.test.mjs:25-33 to include disabled text and the status foregrounds so the narrower claim is fully covered.
findings.verifier_notes: Factually confirmed: CHANGELOG.md:22 is "  header and each passes WCAG AA by test." and apps/shell/test/themes.test.mjs:25-33 checks seven ratios against AA_TEXT 4.5 / AA_LARGE 3, nothing else in apps/shell/test touches keyboard, focus, non-text contrast or reflow. But the test file's own header comment at lines 1-3 scopes it ("Every palette must meet WCAG AA where text sits"), and the claim lives in the `## Unreleased` section of a CHANGELOG that is in neither ssc_race_engineer.spec datas (49-74) nor installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss [Files] (53-69), so it is not a shipped legal or validation artifact. This is an internal wording overreach, not a medium defect. | The technical claim is exactly right. apps/shell/test/themes.test.mjs:26-33 defines a `checks` array of precisely seven entries - textPrimary and textSecondary against body and surface at 4.5:1, onAccent against accent at 4.5:1, and accent against body and surface at 3:1 - which is WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 for a token subset, not conformance to Level AA. Nothing in apps/shell/test/ exercises keyboard operability, focus visibility, non-text contrast, reflow or name/role/value, and disabled/status/warning/error foregrounds are not in the array. CHANGELOG.md:22 still says "each passes WCAG AA by test". Severity corrected down: CHANGELOG.md appears in neither ssc_race_engineer.spec's datas (lines 49-74) nor installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss [Files] (54-68), so this overclaim is not in any shipped artifact, and PRODUCT.md:103 states the same fact correctly. It is a repository-document overstatement, which is low.

findings.title: 1.0.4 release notes and BUILD_INFO describe none of the Electron shell the installer now deploys, under an unchanged VERSION
findings.quote:
# SSC Race Engineer 1.0.4 release candidate

The Control Center is regrouped into Session, Specialist and System pages and
gains a light theme (header button, applied at the next launch) built from the
same verified Astryx Neutral 0.5.2 token pairs as the dark theme.
findings.why_wrong: VERSION still reads 1.0.4, and this file - the only release document shipped to users (installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss:63, ssc_race_engineer.spec:58) - describes only the 2026-09-14 Tk work. Everything this branch adds sits under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md:3-100: the src-layout restructure, the loopback HTTP API, and an entire Electron+React desktop shell that installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss:68 copies to {app}\shell and line 74 gives its own Start-menu entry. README.md:25 sends users to this file for "What changed in this candidate".
findings.impact: Two materially different installers can both be named SSC_Race_Engineer_v1.0.4_Setup.exe - one with a shell, one without, since the .iss makes it conditional on #ifexist (lines 12-13). A teammate cannot tell from the version, the release notes or BUILD_INFO.txt which one they have, and the shipped notes actively mislead them about what got installed.
findings.fix: Bump VERSION to 1.1.0 (a new shipped executable is not a patch), move the `## Unreleased` block in CHANGELOG.md under that heading, and rewrite docs/release/RELEASE_NOTES.md and BUILD_INFO.txt to state that the installer now also places an Electron desktop shell at {app}\shell with its own Start-menu entry and its own licence file.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed. VERSION is "1.0.4"; docs/release/RELEASE_NOTES.md:1-12 describes only the Tk Control Center regroup, light theme, DPI and STOPPING work with no mention of a shell; the shell, src layout and loopback API all sit under `## Unreleased` at CHANGELOG.md:3-30. The file ships via installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss:61 and ssc_race_engineer.spec:58. The two-installers-one-name hazard is real: iss lines 12-14 `#ifexist MyShellDir + "\" + MyShellExe` / `#define HasShell` gate lines 66-69 and 73-75, while OutputBaseFilename (line 32) depends only on MyAppVersion. BUILD_INFO.txt:7 still says the dependency set is "(unchanged)". | The facts hold: VERSION reads 1.0.4, docs/release/RELEASE_NOTES.md:1-19 describes only the Tk Control Center regrouping and light theme and closes with "See VALIDATION_REPORT.txt for source checks", while the shell, the src-layout move and the loopback API are all under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md:3-30. The durable defect is the installer naming: installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss:12-13 `#ifexist MyShellDir + "\" + MyShellExe` / `#define HasShell` makes the shell conditional, but line 32 `OutputBaseFilename=SSC_Race_Engineer_v{#MyAppVersion}_Setup{#MyOutputSuffix}` does not vary with it, so two builds with materially different installed footprints produce byte-different files with identical names. Severity corrected down: holding unreleased work under `## Unreleased` on an unmerged candidate branch is correct changelog practice, not a defect - release notes are written at release. Stripped to the installer-name ambiguity, this is low.

findings.title: Wheel/sdist metadata omits THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt and no package-data rule ships the vendored MIT licence
findings.quote: license-files = ["LICENSE", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"]
findings.why_wrong: `packages` at pyproject.toml:62-76 includes "pyLMUSharedMemory" with package-dir mapping it to third_party/pyLMUSharedMemory, so any wheel built from this project redistributes the vendored MIT modules. But setuptools only puts .py files into a package by default, there is no [tool.setuptools.package-data] table anywhere in pyproject.toml and no MANIFEST.in exists (confirmed by listing the root), so third_party/pyLMUSharedMemory/License.txt is not included. Meanwhile license-files names only LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md - the generated src/ssc_race_engineer.egg-info/PKG-INFO:24-25 confirms exactly two `License-File:` entries, and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt, where the LGPL, GPL, OFL and BSD texts actually live, is absent. CONTRIBUTING.md:24 and .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml:66 both build this project as an installable distribution.
findings.impact: Any wheel or sdist produced from this tree - including the editable install the documented setup path creates - carries MIT-licensed third-party code with neither its licence file nor the licence-text bundle. Anyone who copies that artifact redistributes pyLMUSharedMemory with no permission notice attached, the same defect as the frozen app through a second channel.
findings.fix: Add `license-files = ["LICENSE", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md", "THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt"]` and a [tool.setuptools.package-data] entry `pyLMUSharedMemory = ["License.txt", "README.md"]`, then assert both land in the built wheel from tests/release/test_release_packaging.py.
findings.verifier_notes: Substance confirmed, citation off by one: the quoted `license-files = ["LICENSE", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"]` is pyproject.toml:12, not :11 (line 11 is `license = "LicenseRef-Proprietary"`). packages at 64-78 includes "pyLMUSharedMemory" with package-dir at line 63 mapping it to third_party/pyLMUSharedMemory; there is no [tool.setuptools.package-data] table and no MANIFEST.in (confirmed by ls), and PKG-INFO carries exactly two `License-File:` lines. Severity lowered because no wheel or sdist is actually distributed: the classifier at pyproject.toml:26 is "Private :: Do Not Upload", and both the documented setup and .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml:66 install with `--no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .`, i.e. editable, which redistributes nothing. The shipped-installer instance of this defect is already finding 2. | Every leg verified. pyproject.toml:11 `license-files = ["LICENSE", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"]`; pyproject.toml:63 `package-dir = { "" = "src", "pyLMUSharedMemory" = "third_party/pyLMUSharedMemory" }` with "pyLMUSharedMemory" listed in `packages` (line 75), so the vendored MIT modules go into any built distribution. `grep -n "package-data\|package_data" pyproject.toml` returns nothing and `ls MANIFEST.in` gives "No such file or directory", so setuptools takes .py files only and third_party/pyLMUSharedMemory/License.txt is left out. The generated src/ssc_race_engineer.egg-info/PKG-INFO lines 24-25 confirm exactly two entries, `License-File: LICENSE` and `License-File: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` - THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt, where the LGPL, GPL, OFL and BSD texts live, is absent. Same MIT-condition breach as finding 2 through the packaging channel, and independently confirmed.

findings.title: licenses.mjs crashes with EISDIR on any dependency that ships a licences directory
findings.quote: return readdirSync(dir).filter((entry) => /^(licen[cs]e|copying|notice)/i.test(entry)).map((entry) => path.join(dir, entry));
findings.why_wrong: readdirSync returns directory entries as well as files, and the regex matches names like `licenses/` or `LICENSES/` that several npm packages ship. The result is passed straight to readFileSync(file, "utf8") at line 63 with no statSync/isFile() guard, so a directory entry throws EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory. The Python sibling gets this right - scripts/release/collect_third_party_licenses.py:36 filters with `if path.is_file()`.
findings.impact: Adding any production dependency that ships a licenses/ directory makes `pnpm licenses:write`, `pnpm test` (apps/shell/test/licenses.test.mjs:19 calls render()) and `pnpm package` (apps/shell/scripts/package.mjs:14-15) all fail with an opaque EISDIR trace instead of producing the legal notice, and the CI job at .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml:96-98 dies with no indication that the cause is a licence directory.
findings.fix: Mirror the Python collector: add `.filter((entry) => statSync(path.join(dir, entry)).isFile())` before the map, and recurse one level into any matched directory so packages that keep their texts in licenses/ still contribute their notices rather than being silently skipped.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed. apps/shell/scripts/licenses.mjs:53 is verbatim `return readdirSync(dir).filter((entry) => /^(licen[cs]e|copying|notice)/i.test(entry)).map((entry) => path.join(dir, entry));` with no withFileTypes and no statSync, and line 63 calls `readFileSync(file, "utf8")` on each result inside render(). No try/catch anywhere in the module. The Python counterpart does guard: collect_third_party_licenses.py:36 `return sorted({path for path in candidates if path.is_file()})`. Correctly rated low - it is latent until such a dependency is added. | The code defect is unambiguous. apps/shell/scripts/licenses.mjs:52-54 is `return readdirSync(dir).filter((entry) => /^(licen[cs]e|copying|notice)/i.test(entry)).map((entry) => path.join(dir, entry));` - readdirSync with no withFileTypes returns directory names too, and the regex matches `licenses`/`LICENSES` - and line 63 consumes the result as `files.map((file) => readFileSync(file, "utf8")...)` with no statSync or isFile guard, which throws EISDIR on a directory. The project's own Python equivalent gets it right: collect_third_party_licenses.py:36 ends `return sorted({path for path in candidates if path.is_file()})`. Failure propagates through render() into apps/shell/test/licenses.test.mjs:19 and package.mjs:14-15 (`licenses.mjs --check`, exit on non-zero). Kept at low because no current production dependency (the eight in apps/shell/package.json) ships such a directory, so this is latent until the next dependency addition rather than a live break.

findings.title: README says CI builds the installer on every push; the workflow only runs on pushes to main
findings.quote:
vendored bridge. CI repeats the suite on Python 3.11 to 3.13 and builds the
unsigned installer on every push and pull request.
findings.why_wrong: .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml:3-5 reads `on:` / `push:` / `branches: [main]`. Pushes to any other branch - including the chore/professional-baseline branch this 25,834-line change lives on - trigger nothing. Only pull_request and workflow_dispatch cover other refs. The claim is also load-bearing for the badge at README.md:3, which renders the status of windows-ci.yml on the default branch: that badge reports on origin/main (7b6701d), 53 commits behind this tree, so it says nothing about the candidate the README describes.
findings.impact: A reader of the README, or of the green badge at the top of it, reasonably concludes the code in front of them has passed Windows CI. For this branch nothing has run: no Python suite, no mypy, no locked-release build, no installer, no shell gate. The candidate's central quality claim rests on a badge measuring a different commit.
findings.fix: Correct README.md:121-122 to "on pull requests and on pushes to main", and either add `branches: ['**']` to the push trigger in .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml:4-5 or pin the badge URL to ?branch=main and say so next to it.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed. README.md:120-121 reads "CI repeats the suite on Python 3.11 to 3.13 and builds the / unsigned installer on every push and pull request." .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml:3-7 is `on:` / `push:` / `branches: [main]` / `pull_request:` / `workflow_dispatch:`. The badge at README.md:3 points at that workflow's default-branch status. Note the claim is only half wrong - `pull_request:` is unrestricted, so every PR does build - which is why low is the right rating. | Confirmed verbatim. .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml:3-7 is `on:` / `push:` / `branches: [main]` / `pull_request:` / `workflow_dispatch:`, and README.md:120-121 says CI "builds the unsigned installer on every push and pull request." A push to any non-main branch triggers nothing, so the sentence is false as written. Note the finding's impact paragraph overreaches - `pull_request:` carries no branch filter, so a PR opened from chore/professional-baseline would run the full matrix, mypy, the locked build and the installer; it is not true that "nothing has run" for this work in principle. The README inaccuracy and the badge-measures-a-different-commit point both stand at low.

findings.title: THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt header names a generator path that has not existed since the tree rework

The committed file's line 3 reads "Generated by scripts/collect_third_party_licenses.py from the hash-locked", while the generator's own header literal at scripts/release/collect_third_party_licenses.py:78-82 emits "Generated by scripts/release/collect_third_party_licenses.py from the hash-locked". The freshness gap is real too: tests/release/test_third_party_licenses.py:14-22 only asserts `f"\n{component['name']} {component['version']}  [" not in text` for each SBOM component, so licence-body drift passes as long as names and versions are unchanged - unlike the shell, whose apps/shell/test/licenses.test.mjs:18-20 asserts full equality with `render()`.

findings.title: Shipped feature docs contain em-dashes that CONTRIBUTING forbids in shipped documents
findings.quote: # LICO background runtime — checkpoint C work in progress
findings.why_wrong: CONTRIBUTING.md:142 states "No em-dashes, no local paths, no personal names in shipped documents", and PRODUCT.md:81-82 repeats it as a brand commitment ("no hype; no em-dashes"). ssc_race_engineer.spec:70-74 globs every .md under docs/features and docs/architecture into the frozen app, so these are shipped documents by the project's own definition (docs/README.md:21-23: "a document ships only if one of them names it or its folder"). findings.title: SECURITY.md gives no reachable contact channel for a private repository
findings.quote:
Do not open a public issue for a vulnerability. Contact the repository owner
directly (`@Leodrifts` on GitHub) with:
findings.why_wrong: The only contact route offered is a GitHub handle. The repository is private (pyproject.toml:25 sets the `Private :: Do Not Upload` classifier and pyproject.toml:29 points at github.com/Leodrifts/SSC-Race-Engineer), so a reporter who is not already a collaborator cannot see the repo, cannot open a private security advisory on it, and has no address, PGP key or form to use. There is no .github security contact, no email anywhere in the file, and no private vulnerability reporting configuration in .github/. The 7-day acknowledgement promise at line 25 is made with no channel capable of delivering the report.
findings.impact: The audience this policy explicitly invites - people testing the credential handling, the Ed25519 update path and the team gateway (lines 8-11) - includes evaluators and teammates who are not repo collaborators. They have no way to reach the maintainer, so a real finding about credential handling or the signed-update trust boundary has no route in, and will surface publicly or not at all.
findings.fix: Add a monitored security email address (or a form on the existing team-gateway) to SECURITY.md:18-23, and enable GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting on the repository so the advisory flow works for anyone granted read access.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed by reading SECURITY.md in full. Line 18-19 is the only contact route: "Contact the repository owner / directly (`@Leodrifts` on GitHub)". There is no email, no PGP key, no form, and GitHub offers no direct-message facility, so a non-collaborator has nothing to use; the repository is private per pyproject.toml:26 ("Private :: Do Not Upload") and :30. The 7-day acknowledgement at line 25 is therefore unbacked. The scope section at lines 8-11 does invite exactly the non-collaborator audience the finder describes. | The audience the finding constructs never reaches this document. SECURITY.md is not distributed: `grep -rn "SECURITY.md" ssc_race_engineer.spec installer/SSC_Race_Engineer.iss` returns nothing, and it is absent from the spec's datas list (lines 49-74) and the installer's [Files] (54-68). It lives only in the private GitHub repository, whose readers are collaborators by definition - and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml sets `blank_issues_enabled: true` and links the policy from the issue chooser, so a collaborator reading "Do not open a public issue" can file a non-public issue in the private repo, use the private advisory flow, or reach @Leodrifts via .github/CODEOWNERS. The scenario of "an evaluator who is not a collaborator" is a person who has the installer, which does not contain SECURITY.md, so they never see the 7-day promise the finding says cannot be honoured. No concrete report is stranded by this file.

findings.title: Lighthouse evidence harness cannot run: server script resolves repo root one directory short
findings.quote: const repo = process.argv[2] ?? path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
findings.why_wrong: The script lives at scripts/dev/, so path.dirname(...) + ".." resolves to <repo>/scripts, not <repo>. Line 6 then imports `${repo}/services/team-gateway/src/mobile.js`, i.e. <repo>/scripts/services/team-gateway/src/mobile.js, which does not exist. The only caller, scripts/dev/lighthouse_mobile_pit_wall.ps1:12, computes `$repo = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot` (= <repo>\scripts) and passes that same wrong value explicitly at line 22, so the argv[2] path is broken identically. Both were written before the restructure moved these two files from scripts/ into scripts/dev/ and neither `..` was updated.
findings.impact: I ran it: `node scripts/dev/serve_mobile_pit_wall.mjs` -> `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '/home/user/ssc-race-engineer/scripts/services/team-gateway/src/mobile.js'`. The HTTP server never starts, so lighthouse_mobile_pit_wall.ps1 audits nothing, prints "mobile : no report" / "desktop : no report" and exits 1. VALIDATION_REPORT.txt:8 nevertheless ships inside the application asserting "Mobile pit wall Lighthouse 13.4.1: 100/100/100/100 on mobile and desktop presets" — a headline release claim whose only producing tool is incapable of running on the commit that ships the claim. The reports would land in outputs/, which .gitignore:77 excludes, so no artifact can contradict it either.
findings.fix: Change line 5 to resolve `"../.."`, and change lighthouse_mobile_pit_wall.ps1:12 to `$repo = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)`. Then re-run the audit and either reproduce the 100/100/100/100 figures or strike them from VALIDATION_REPORT.txt.

findings.title: Traffic LICO native overlay can never locate the source tree after the src-layout move
findings.quote: if (Directory.Exists(Path.Combine(dir.FullName, "ssc_engineer", "lico"))) return dir.FullName;
findings.why_wrong: LocateRoot() walks ancestors looking for `<dir>/ssc_engineer/lico`. On this branch the package lives at `src/ssc_engineer/lico` — there is no `ssc_engineer` directory at any ancestor level (I checked: `ls -d ssc_engineer` fails, only `src/ssc_engineer` exists). The same staleness appears twice more in the file: line 232 maps the dev asset host to `Path.Combine(root, "traffic-lico", "ui", "dist")` when the directory is now `apps/traffic-lico/ui/dist`, and line 324 spawns `Path.Combine(root, "work", "lico", environment, "Scripts", "python.exe")` while Build.ps1:23 creates those venvs under `$licoRepo\work\lico\...` where `$licoRepo = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent` = `<repo>/apps`.
findings.impact: Running the overlay unpackaged (the only way to run it, since it is absent from the installer) throws `DirectoryNotFoundException("Launch Traffic LICO from its SSC source folder.")` from LocateRoot before the window ever opens; Program.cs:59 turns that into a MessageBox reading "Repair or reinstall SSC Race Engineer if files are missing." — advice that cannot help, because the real cause is a path constant nobody updated.
